'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Islamic State insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|Islamic State insurgency in Iraq]]
**Eight civilians are killed and many more wounded after [[Islamic State]] gunmen open fire against a convoy carrying villagers in [[Albu Bali]], [[Al Anbar Governorate]]. [https://english.almayadeen.net/news/politics/iraq:-several-killed-wounded-in-isis-attack-in-albu-bali (Al Mayadeen)]
*[[2022 Jordanian protests]]
**Three police officers and a gunman are killed during a raid on the hideout of the suspected killers of a policeman during protests in [[Ma'an]], [[Jordan]]. Nine people are arrested. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/12/19/three-jordanian-police-killed-during-raid-on-hideout-in-maan (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Two civilians and a soldier are killed and another civilian is wounded during a [[Suicide attack|suicide bombing]] in [[Miranshah]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://english.news.cn/20221220/e5bcede9b4f64352b47ea84d15743417/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Four [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] members are killed by gunmen in [[Saravan, Iran|Saravan]], [[Iran]], near the [[Iran–Pakistan border|border with Pakistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/12/19/irgc-says-four-security-forces-killed-near-pakistan-border (Al Jazeera)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2021–2022 global energy crisis]]
**[[EU natural gas price cap]]
***[[European Union]] member states agree to a [[natural gas]] [[EU natural gas price cap|price cap]] in an attempt to limit economic damage from the [[2021–2022 global energy crisis|global energy crisis]]. The price cap can be triggered beginning on February 15, if for three days, prices on the [[Dutch Title Transfer Facility|TTF]], which is the European natural gas benchmark, exceed [[euro|€]]180 per [[megawatt-hour]] (MWh) and are also more than €35/MWh higher than a reference price based on [[liquefied natural gas]] price assessments. [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/eu-countries-make-final-push-gas-price-cap-deal-this-year-2022-12-19/ (Reuters)]
*Aftermath of the [[Ethiopia–Tigray peace agreement]]
**The [[Commercial Bank of Ethiopia]], [[Ethiopia|the country]]'s largest [[commercial bank]], resumes operations in some [[Tigray Region|Tigrayan]] cities and towns following the suspension of services during the [[Tigray War]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/business-and-tech/20221219-ethiopia-s-largest-bank-says-tigray-services-resume (AFP via RFI)]
'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Five people are killed and nine others are injured after a building collapses in [[Kilimanjaro Region]], [[Tanzania]]. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2022/12/20/five-killed-after-building-collapses-in-tanzania (The Star)]
'''Law and crime'''
*[[Rwanda asylum plan]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United Kingdom|High Court of the United Kingdom]] rules that the [[British government]]'s plan to send [[asylum seeker]]s to [[Rwanda]] while their application is ongoing is lawful. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/12/19/uk/uk-rwanda-policy-ruling-gbr-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack]]
**The [[January 6th Committee]] issues a report in its final meeting declaring that former [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] was the "central cause" of the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|January 6]] [[United States Capitol]] attack, and recommends that he be referred to the [[United States Department of Justice|Justice Department]] for prosecution on at least four criminal charges. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/jan-6-committee-condemns-trump-central-cause-insurrection/story?id=95552986 (ABC News)]
*[[Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse cases]]
**American film producer [[Harvey Weinstein]] is convicted on 3 of 7 sexual assault charges against him. The jury found Weinstein either not guilty, or was hung, on four other charges. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/12/19/us/harvey-weinstein-trial-deliberations-los-angeles-monday/index.html (CNN)]
